findings.evidence: public record CurrencyRevenue(String currency, BigDecimal current, BigDecimal previous, Double changePct, TrendValue paidOrders, List<MonthlyAmount> monthly)  and  public record MonthlyAmount(String month, BigDecimal amount, boolean partial)  -- Javadoc: 'Amounts are exact and always per currency'. No @JsonFormat/@JsonSerialize on the fields and no spring.jackson.* override (grep of resources: none), so Jackson writes a JSON number (phase-04-test-report.json OBS-P4-003: 'jsonPath numeric match 1500000.5'). Order.amount is numeric(19,2) (Order.java:37) and a sum of untouched rows keeps scale 2 ('1500000.00') while zero-filled slots are BigDecimal.ZERO ('0').
findings.why_it_matters: The backend arithmetic is exact (SUM over numeric in PostgreSQL, BigDecimal end to end, percentChange on BigDecimal, cache round trip proven beyond double precision), but the wire format is a JSON number that every JS client parses as an IEEE double. This is safe today: plans are restricted to VND (PlanRequest.java:31 @Pattern(regexp = "VND"), BillingConstants.PAYOS_CURRENCY = "VND", OrderService.validatePayOsAmount), VND is a zero-decimal currency, and a per-currency sum would need to exceed 2^53 (about 9.0e15 VND) to lose a unit, six orders of magnitude above any realistic platform revenue. It stops being safe the day a currency with fractional digits is enabled (0.1 style values are not representable) or a figure ever crosses 2^53, and the Javadoc 'exact' does not tell the Phase 5 author that exactness ends at the wire. Severity LOW: no defect with current data, only an undocumented contract limit that the multi-currency design invites to be exceeded.
findings.required_action: Non-blocking. Recommendation: KEEP JSON numbers for Phase 4/5 (VND-only, zero decimals; strings or minor units would be a gratuitous contract complication now). (1) Reword the AdminSectionData Javadoc to 'exact in the backend; delivered as a JSON number, safe up to 2^53' and record the VND-only assumption. (2) Phase 5 types current/previous/amount as number and formats with Intl.NumberFormat using the row's currency fraction digits, never sums across currencies, never re-derives changePct. (3) Make it a hard precondition of enabling any non-VND currency (relaxing the PlanRequest/PlanUpdateRequest VND pattern) to switch these three BigDecimal fields to string serialization (@JsonFormat(shape = JsonFormat.Shape.STRING), which round-trips through the typed DashboardCache read unchanged) or to minor-unit longs, together with a Phase 5 client change. Optionally normalise the scale on the wire (setScale(2)) so 'ZERO' and '1500000.00' are not mixed in one payload.

findings.evidence: Billing now exposes two dashboard facades: BillingOverviewService (tenant host + platform commercial counts, 5 repositories, 243 lines) and BillingRevenueOverviewService (OrderRepository only, 79 lines). The plan Design Constraint says 'Extend existing billing and item bank facades'; the plan Preflight records the deliberate deviation (new root facades because ItembankService is 806 lines and BillingOverviewService is near the limit). Every other module has exactly one *OverviewService.
findings.why_it_matters: The deviation is justified and follows the Phase 3 QUAL-004 advice: each new class has a one-sentence responsibility (online paid-order revenue per currency; item bank dashboard counts), is self-contained (own repository only, nested records, no enum or entity leak, no new dependency), and adding revenue to BillingOverviewService would have pushed it past 300 lines (243 + ~75). The only cost is that 'billing dashboard reads' now live in two places with nothing pointing from one to the other. Convention is consistent in naming (<Module>OverviewService / <Module><Topic>OverviewService) and in shape (nested public records at the module root, @Transactional(readOnly = true) per method, constructor DI, no unused imports).
findings.required_action: None required. Optionally add one Javadoc sentence to BillingOverviewService stating that platform revenue is owned by BillingRevenueOverviewService, so the split is discoverable.

findings.evidence: series = billing.paidAmountsPerRange(boundaries); current = byCurrency(billing.paidRevenueBetween(w.start(), w.end())); previous = byCurrency(billing.paidRevenueBetween(...)); currencies = TreeSet(series.keySet()) + current.keySet() + previous.keySet(); series.getOrDefault(currency, emptySeries). Each facade method is its own @Transactional(readOnly = true), so the three reads are three snapshots.
findings.why_it_matters: The union rule is sound and correct for every normal case: currencies are the ordered union (a currency present only in older months, only in a window, or only in the series is listed; absent window amounts are zero, never a fabricated percentage because previous = 0 yields changePct null), 12 buckets end with the partial current month in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, amounts are never added across currencies, only PAID + deleted = false rows with paidAt in [from, to) are read. Because the windows are at most 90 + 90 days the 12-month series always covers them, so the union with the window keys is redundant defence. The only gap is a payment committing between the series query and the window queries: a currency can then appear with a window amount and an all-zero monthly series for at most one 60 s cache TTL. Cosmetic and self-healing.
findings.required_action: None. If exact internal consistency is ever required, read the three facts in one facade call/transaction.

findings.evidence: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_paid_at ON orders (paid_at) WHERE status = 'PAID' AND deleted = false;  vs  '... o.status = :status AND o.paidAt >= :from AND o.paidAt < :to GROUP BY o.currency' with OrderStatus.PAID bound as a parameter. phase-04-explain-plans.txt:14-29,235-258: default planner Index Scan idx_orders_paid_at for window/month shapes (0.4-1.9 ms), prepared with bound parameters plan_cache_mode=auto still Index Scan, force_generic_plan degrades to Bitmap Heap Scan idx_orders_status_created 11.3-15.6 ms; whole 14-statement load 27.7 ms with vs 151.7-176.3 ms without the index at 100k orders; question bank counts Seq Scan + HashAggregate 14.8 ms and created-in-window Seq Scan 8.4 ms at 40k rows.
findings.why_it_matters: V97 verdict: KEEP and justified by evidence (about 6x, grows linearly). It is idempotent, additive and backward compatible (old and new app versions both work, either deploy order), partial on exactly the rows read, header documents rollback (drop the index), same shape as V93-V96, plain CREATE INDEX (not CONCURRENTLY) like its siblings: a brief write lock on a small orders table. The one residual: a partial index is usable only when the planner knows status = 'PAID' at plan time, so it depends on custom plans (the default). QuestionRepository's own generation queries inline the enum literal for exactly this reason; the new OrderRepository query passes it as a parameter. The 14-statement miss (2 windows + 12 months, about 1 ms each) is acceptable behind the 60 s section cache; the question bank sequential scans are inherent to counting every shared question and carry no timeout hint, linear in bank size (tens of thousands expected).
findings.required_action: None. Optional hardening: inline com.pte.billing.domain.enums.OrderStatus.PAID as a JPQL literal (like QuestionRepository.java:112) so the partial index does not depend on plan_cache_mode. Revisit one grouped-by-month statement and a questions(created_at) index only if orders pass ~1M rows or the bank passes ~1M rows.

findings.evidence: String key = DashboardCacheKeys.admin(visibility.bucket(), window.days(), section.key()); ... cache.getOrCompute(key, OverviewConstants.ADMIN_SECTION_TTL, type, loader)  after  if (!visibility.allows(section)) { return DashboardSection.forbidden(); }.  CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION is still "v1".
findings.why_it_matters: Security review result for the new sections (no defect): (a) revenue is gated by AdminSection.REVENUE -> PlatformOperationPolicy.can(caller, COMMERCIAL_READ) (AdminSection.java:24) and the forbidden branch returns before the cache key is built, so a forbidden section is never read from, written to or computed; (b) the bucket is the computed, sorted set of allowed keys: operations callers (admin and manager, both hold COMMERCIAL_READ) get the 10-key string, academic callers (ACADEMIC_MANAGER, ACADEMIC_STAFF, legacy PLATFORM_AUTHOR canonicalised) get exactly 'questionBank', callers who see nothing (tenant-bound or role-less) get 'none' and never reach a cache or facade; the section name is also part of the key, so even a shared bucket could not return another section's payload; the same questionBank payload is simply cached once per bucket (extra small query per 60 s per bucket). QUESTION_BANK uses isPlatformCaller (userId != null, tenantId == null, hasValidScope = platform role xor tenant role), the controller adds the five-role @PreAuthorize and rejects tenant-bound callers with 403; no operations payload ever reaches an academic caller. (c) Schema version decision: NO bump needed and none was needed: every existing section record is unchanged, the two new sections are new keys, and the operations bucket string changed (8 -> 10 keys) while the academic bucket moved none -> questionBank, so entries written by an older instance during a rolling deploy sit under different keys and are never deserialised by the new shape (and vice versa). Remaining carry-forward lifecycle costs (Phase 3 QUAL-007): no single-flight on expiry, windowDays in the key of window-independent sections, a thundering herd of the heaviest query on expiry.
findings.required_action: None. Bump CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION only when an existing cached record changes shape; record that rule next to the constant.

verification_notes.correctness: Per currency only: GROUP BY currency, facade maps keyed by currency, TreeMap/TreeSet by code, amounts never added across currencies (only order counts are added for the top-level paidOrders trend, documented as counts). PAID only: OrderStatus.PAID bound plus deleted = false; the status enum has only PENDING/PAID/CANCELLED/EXPIRED (no refunds), guarded by a test. Windows are half-open on paidAt (>= from, < to) for current [start, end), previous [previousStart, start) and every month bucket; month boundaries come from MonthBuckets.boundaries with Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh (OverviewConstants.BUCKET_ZONE_ID), 12 buckets (SERIES_MONTHS), last flagged partial in toAmountPoints. Amounts: SUM of numeric(19,2) returns BigDecimal exactly; toAmount() fallback only for non-BigDecimal drivers. percentChange(current, previous): (current - previous) * 100 / previous, scale 1, HALF_UP, null when previous.signum() == 0 (any scale) -> identical semantics to the long variant, which now calls it (single source). Currency set = TreeSet union of series, current and previous keys; zero amounts for absent windows and an all-zero 12-point series for a currency with none (see QUAL-004 for the multi-snapshot caveat). Question bank counts the same rows as the old stats: visibility SHARED, deleted = false, every revision (superseded revision is ARCHIVED, publish flow ItembankService.java:384-389), task_type_section NOT NULL (no null map key), enum keys zero-filled (status, section, pool); bySection also keeps unknown stored section names; total = sum of the grouped counts. The old stats method/endpoint are untouched (ItembankService.stats at 238-251 still uses countBySectionAndVisibility, countByStatusAndVisibility, countByDeletedFalseAndVisibility). approvedByPool is an extra field beyond the plan steps but is the direct answer to the plan Risk 'expose the pool split so the UI can label correctly' (byPool counts all statuses; approvedByPool is the EXAM vs PRACTICE split of approved stock, and an APPROVED row is always current because publish demotes the superseded revision); acceptable, one map, no extra query, documented in both Javadocs, not scope creep. No approval-time trend is promised: AdminSectionData.QuestionBank Javadoc and ItembankOverviewService Javadoc state it, and no approved_at/published_at column exists on questions (grep of itembank domain and migrations: only task-type definition/usage timestamps), so createdInWindow (created-at) is the honest trend.
